bull.b: The sharp TTM revenue increase and return to positive net income and EBITDA show meaningful recent operating improvement. If sustained, this larger revenue base can support investment in the pipeline, improve operating leverage, and strengthen Zymeworks’ ability to fund growth.

The Roche agreement validates Zymeworks’ multispecific antibody technology while shifting later development, manufacturing, and commercialization costs to a larger partner. Upfront cash, milestone opportunities, and royalties provide potentially durable non-dilutive funding and broader market access.

Ziihera’s expanded FDA-approved use and resulting milestone demonstrate that Zymeworks can convert development assets into meaningful economic benefits. Higher revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance also indicate a stronger near-term commercial foundation for its broader portfolio.

bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that reported earnings are not yet translating into internally generated cash. Continued burn can require external financing or milestone timing to support development, limiting flexibility and making financial sustainability more dependent on future cash inflows.

The substantial increase in absolute debt reduces balance-sheet flexibility and raises the financial obligations that must be serviced alongside clinical and commercial investment. Greater leverage can constrain future capital allocation and make the business more sensitive to weaker operating results.

Although recent net income and EBITDA improved, the history of large operating losses and negative TTM return on equity shows that profitability has not yet become consistent. This weakens confidence that current earnings represent a durable operating level across development and commercialization cycles.
